38	holds slot `k+1` it holds slot `k`. "Op 11 admitted while op 10 is delayed"
39	is unreachable inside an epoch for an honest author and self-inflicted for a
40	Byzantine one. Every part of the superseded grammar that existed to represent
41	an admitted-above-gap slot (`already-present`, `coveredStateDigest`,
42	`semanticIdentityDigest`, replacement references, `zero-intent`,
43	`settlement-control`, `hasDisplacedOperation`) is deleted. The author's own
44	authenticated boundary from the checkpoint tells it exactly which of its rows
45	were admitted (at or below the boundary) and which were not (above it).

47	### What the construction is
48	
49	1. A **durable settlement plan** in the author's issuance store, written before
50	   any issue after open/adopt, recording one disposition per displaced source
51	   and linked atomically to the fence and each replacement inside the existing
52	   `transactIssue` transaction.
53	2. An **author fence** control operation `$drp.author-fence.v1` carrying one
54	   integer `fenceSequence = m`, issued **first** after the plan; every
55	   replacement is issued **after** it and therefore causally follows it.
56	3. A creator-signed **settlement checkpoint** whose frontier is
57	   `[author, admissionEpoch, terminalThrough]` for exactly the successor ACL's
58	   members, with `admissionEpoch` derived from the ACL diff and carried only
59	   in the checkpoint. No retired-author registry, no `sequenceFloor`, no
60	   `admittedThrough`, no ACL member-record change, no issuance-store scope change, no
61	   lineage jump.
62	
63	The construction is the Kafka producer-epoch / Zab ballot / MLS epoch fencing
64	pattern adapted so `authorSequence` stays never-resetting on each device. It
65	adds no cryptography, no wire-envelope field and no external trust service.
66	It adds one issuance-store object store (schema bump), one control operation
67	inside the existing v3 envelope, and one closure record kind.

69	## Settlement checkpoint
70	
71	Kind `drp-creator-author-settlement-state`, version `1`, domain
72	`ts-drp/creator-author-settlement/v1`, maximum 32,768 canonical bytes
73	(D.110c-0c1k stage W1; measured 23,937 bytes at 256 max-width triples):
74	
75	```ts
76	{
77		closedAnchorDigest, closedEpoch, commitQcRef: { byteLength, digest },
78		currentAclDigest, cutValueDigest,
79		frontiers: readonly [author: string, admissionEpoch: number, terminalThrough: number | null][],
80		genesisAnchorDigest, historyRoot, historySize,
81		kind: "drp-creator-author-settlement-state", objectId,
82		priorCheckpointDigest, priorCheckpointKind: "genesis" | "settled-v1",
83		protocolMajor: 3, snapshotManifestDigest, successorAclDigest,
84		successorAnchorDigest, successorEpoch, version: 1,
85	}
86	```
87	
88	- `frontiers` are strictly code-unit sorted, unique, and exactly the successor
89	  ACL's members of every role (at most 256). A member present in the prior
90	  checkpoint carries its `admissionEpoch` unchanged and a monotone
91	  `terminalThrough` (`null → n` allowed; `n → null` or lower rejected). A member absent from the **current ACL** (added at this close) carries
92	  `admissionEpoch = successorEpoch` and `terminalThrough = null`. When the
93	  predecessor is the genesis sentinel, members of the current (genesis) ACL
94	  receive `admissionEpoch = 0` and members added at this close receive
95	  `successorEpoch`. The verifier recomputes membership from the two bound ACL
96	  digests; "absent from the prior checkpoint" is never the key.
97	- The record binds the current and successor anchors and ACLs, cut, commit QC,
98	  snapshot manifest, history root/size and pinned genesis exactly as the
99	  superseded design did; any mismatch fails closed.
100	- **Signing and verification (signer-agnostic).** The record carries
101	  `detachedAuthoritySignature`. Prepare mints the opaque signing request under
102	  the **successor** trust material's public key; open verifies under floor
103	  trust only. The codec never compares a current-epoch key to the successor or
104	  floor key; the checks at
105	  `packages/protocol-v3/src/creator-author-issuance-frontiers.ts:278` and
106	  `:399` are not carried over. The closing epoch is bound by
107	  `closedAnchorDigest`, `closedEpoch`, `currentAclDigest` and `commitQcRef`,
108	  not by signer identity. Under `creator-trusted-settlement-v1` both keys
109	  coincide, so behavior is identical; the rule exists so the checkpoint is a
110	  payload of the authority that installs epoch N+1 and composes unchanged with
111	  a later rotated-authority lineage profile (`D.110c-0c1j`).
112	- **Predecessor rules and where they run.** The opener verifies one record
113	  against floor trust and the expected cut/QC/manifest/ACL digests;
114	  `priorCheckpointDigest`/`priorCheckpointKind` are validated for shape only.
115	  Adjacency (genesis sentinel or exactly one adjacent `settled-v1`),
116	  `admissionEpoch` copy-unchanged and `terminalThrough` monotonicity are
117	  enforced by the control-plane bounded-advance predicate over the retained
118	  immediate predecessor inside the D.110c-0b rollback window. No opener, cold
119	  or hot, walks the checkpoint chain; cold reopen is O(1) in epochs.
120	- The codec exports `frontierFor(identity, author)` and
121	  `frontierCount(identity)`; consumers outside protocol-v3 use them rather than
122	  indexing `frontiers`. This is the only preparation for a later map-backed
123	  carrier (`D.110c-0c1k`); no field is reserved.
124	- f5b0a measures the 256-member maximum shape (about 23,937 bytes at maximum
125	  integer widths; 6,593 bytes at 64) and pins it plus the 257-line and
126	  32,769-byte rejections as executable vectors. The cap and ceiling come from
127	  D.110c-0c1k stage W1 (`.logs/d110c-0c1k-fable51-research-20260903/solution.md`
128	  §3), which found that no flat vector reaches Profile D's 128 distinct authors
129	  under an 8,192-byte ceiling (crossing at 89 members at maximum widths).

131	## Fence carrier
132	
133	```ts
134	type AuthorFenceOperation = Readonly<{
135		action: "$drp.author-fence.v1";
136		fenceSequence: number; // m: safe nonnegative integer, m <= outer authorSequence
137		version: 1;
138	}>;
139	```
140	
141	Signed by the outer vertex's author under the existing `ts-drp/vertex/v3`
142	domain at outer slot `f`, it means: "every slot of mine with sequence `< m` in
143	my current incarnation is either already admitted or abandoned and may never
144	be admitted; every slot `>= m` is current-epoch work." The only grammar rule is
145	`m <= f`; there is no bound on `m`, no source list, no replacement reference,
146	no supersession record. Protocol-v3 reserves the action globally (blueprint
147	preparation rejects a blueprint that registers it) and Node recognizes it by
148	its own `action` data property. Admission authority is ACL membership of any
149	role; the operation never reaches a blueprint reducer. The Node close-graph
150	split (application ⊔ control, complete maps for index, charges, frontier,
151	close-set, history and creator scanning; application subset only for the
152	fold) and the dedicated control issuer are retained from the superseded design.
153	
154	## Creator scan at close
155	
156	For each successor ACL member `A`, from the prior frontier
157	`(admissionEpoch = e, terminalThrough = s)` or `(successorEpoch, null)` for a
158	member absent from the current ACL:
159	
160	1. Group `A`'s vertices in the complete current close graph by exact
161	   `(authorSequence, digest)`. A same-slot duplicate freezes `A` at `s`; a
162	   foreign-author slot at or below `s` freezes `A` at `s`; a creator-own
163	   regression keeps its existing fail-closed error
164	   (`packages/node/src/creator-close.ts:486-497`, `:528-546`).
165	2. Among `A`'s fence vertices take the largest `m` with `m <= f` and
166	   (`s === null` or `m > s`); set `s := m − 1` (`m = 0` means the base is before slot 0; by contiguity
167	   the fence's own slot then advances `s` to at least 0 in step 4, so a
168	   negative `terminalThrough` is never emitted). Invalid fences are ignored; nothing aborts.
169	3. If `s === null` and no valid fence exists, scan from slot 0 if it is in the
170	   graph; otherwise emit `null`. This replaces, under the settlement profile,
171	   the close-aborting throw `D110C_0C1F1_AUTHOR_REENTRY_PROOF_REQUIRED`
172	   (`packages/node/src/creator-close.ts:517-524`); `creator-trusted-v1` keeps
173	   that throw byte-for-byte.
174	4. Advance `s` across exactly adjacent graph slots; never take an observed
175	   maximum; never cross an unknown slot.
176	5. Emit `[A, e, s]`.
177	
178	Removed members are dropped from the vector; nothing is remembered about them.
179	The close proceeds when any foreign boundary cannot advance (f5a per-author
180	liveness). Settlement-profile closures emit neither the v1 admitted-frontier
181	aggregate nor the legacy creator-retirement record; the creator's own rows
182	take the same fence path.

184	## Author drain, plan and fence
185	
186	At open or adopt under the settlement profile, before any ordinary issue (the
187	existing rebase startup barrier, `examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2796-2990`,
188	`:3844`, remains the public-issue barrier):
189	
190	1. Read own `(e, s)` from the authenticated checkpoint. A key absent from the
191	   vector is not a member and may not issue.
192	2. Classify every own durable row regardless of `publishState` (replacing the pending-only predicate at `v3-live.ts:6447`, whose
193	   published-skip at `:6446` is the historical defect, and the
194	   published-must-be-present path at `examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2852-2857`), authenticating by own
195	   signature, scope and row digest against the anchor/epoch decoded from the
196	   row (the shape at `v3-live.ts:4762-4769`, not the single-predecessor
197	   classifier at `:4611-4619`), for any `epoch < current`:
198	   - `seq <= s`: terminal (never republished, rebased, applied or used as
199	     evidence);
200	   - `row.epoch < e`: old incarnation, terminal (its content is resubmittable
201	     by the application);
202	   - `row.epoch < current` and `seq > s`: not admitted (contiguity), displaced;
203	   - `row.epoch === current`: current; recovery replays it.
204	   Control rows are never handed to the application; a displaced fence is
205	   superseded by the next fence. Reserved `join`/`causalJoin` rows are covered
206	   by the fence with no application effect. A displaced `acl` row is surfaced
207	   to the application before any fence is issued.
208	3. Build or merge the plan: one entry per displaced application source with the
209	   room's policy (`expire | rebase | transform | manual-review`). Entries that
210	   already carry a `replacementSequence` are fulfilled; a replacement row that
211	   is itself displaced becomes a new source entry; a displaced fence clears `fenceSequence`. An entry whose source row now
212	   classifies terminal (`seq <= s`, or `row.epoch < e`) is removed from the
213	   plan at merge (the boundary, not the plan, settled it) and no longer holds
214	   the prune gate or a `manual-review` hold. Write it with `transactWriteSettlementPlan` (CAS on
215	   `revision`) **before any issue**.
216	4. If any entry is `manual-review`: no fence, no replacements; the barrier
217	   holds; only this author's boundary stalls.
218	5. Issue the fence through the dedicated control issuer with
219	   `m = lineage.next` and `planEffect: { kind: "fence" }`. Node refuses a fence
220	   unless a durable plan exists with no `manual-review` entry and a null
221	   `fenceSequence`. Publish it. A fence is issued at every open/adopt under
222	   the profile once the drain completes, including with an empty plan (a
223	   returning member whose only old rows are terminal old-incarnation rows);
224	   Node's refusal rule accepts a durable empty-entries plan.
225	6. Issue each `rebase`/`transform` replacement as an ordinary application
226	   vertex with `planEffect: { kind: "replacement", sourceSequence }`; the link
227	   is durable in the same transaction as the row. `expire` entries need no
228	   issue.
229	7. The plan is complete when `fenceSequence` is set and every non-`expire`
230	   entry is linked. No source row is ever marked complete; sources become
231	   terminal through the next checkpoint. `completeRebaseSource`
232	   (`v3-live.ts:6637-6685`; room callers `examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2814`,
233	   `:2971`) is unreachable under the profile.
234	
235	Restart at any point re-runs 1-7 from durable truth. The idempotence key is
236	the plan entry; the fence is re-issued only if `fenceSequence` is null or the
237	linked fence row is classified displaced. The complete crash walk that selects
238	this order over replacement-first is `plan-change.md` §A.3: with the fence
239	first, every replacement causally follows it, so "above `terminalThrough`
240	implies not admitted" holds at every instant; replacement-first breaks that
241	whenever the fence is delayed past a close, even without a crash.

292	## ACL transition law
293	
294	- Retained member (present in both ACLs, any role): frontier copied with its
295	  scanned `terminalThrough` and unchanged `admissionEpoch`. Losing or gaining a
296	  role changes nothing in the vector.
297	- Removed member: dropped. Its unadmitted rows are dead to the protocol; its
298	  device keeps them; their content is resubmittable after re-admission.
299	- Added member (fresh or returning, indistinguishable and irrelevant):
300	  `[author, successorEpoch, null]`. Its first accountable vertex is a fence or
301	  slot 0. Local lineage continues on a returning device and starts at 0 on a
302	  fresh device; neither needs a store operation, and neither can collide with
303	  the old incarnation because every old-incarnation vertex is bound to an
304	  epoch below `admissionEpoch` and to a dead anchor, which ingress already
305	  rejects (`v3-live.ts:3800-3829`).
306	- `LatchedAclMember` stays `{author, finalityKey, groups}`
307	  (`packages/protocol-v3/src/latched-acl.ts:8`); snapshot versions 1 and 2 are
308	  untouched. Under the settlement profile the ACL is a version-3 snapshot that
309	  changes only constants (member cap 256, canonical ceiling 65,536 bytes,
310	  decode limits `{maxBytes: 65_536, maxDepth: 4, maxItems: 8_192}`), accepted
311	  only when `settlementProfileFor(profileId) !== "none"`; the author-list cap
312	  at `packages/protocol-v3/src/index.ts:774` rises to 256 under the same
313	  predicate (D.110c-0c1k W1). Staging enforces exactly the open path's decode
314	  limits (D.110c-0c1k W0). The incarnation is a checkpoint fact. Authority membership
315	  (profile/signer-set carriers) and application membership (latched ACL) remain
316	  separate; a player join is an ACL grant and never an authority change.

318	## Recovery, terminal rule and pruning
319	
320	- Under a verified settlement checkpoint any same-author row at or below
321	  `terminalThrough` is terminal regardless of digest; the checkpoint
322	  authenticates a decision boundary, not membership of arbitrary row bytes.
323	  Same-slot equivocation remains evidence and cannot advance a boundary.
324	- Rows above the boundary from an older epoch of the current incarnation
325	  (`admissionEpoch <= epoch < current`) are displaced sources for the plan;
326	  they are never silently terminal. Old-incarnation rows
327	  (`epoch < admissionEpoch`) are terminal at re-admission and covered by the
328	  first fence.
329	- f5b0d adds the storage-neutral `pruneAuthenticatedSettledPrefix` contract
330	  from the superseded design unchanged in shape (compare-and-delete across any
331	  number of old epochs, monotone pruned watermark, expected lineage-next and
332	  prior watermark, partial deletion fails closed), plus the plan gate above,

378	## Crash, attack and failure matrix
379	
380	| Boundary or attack | Required result |
381	| --- | --- |
382	| crash before plan durable | restart re-drains; nothing issued twice |
383	| plan durable, crash before fence | restart issues the fence once |
384	| fence durable, unpublished | restart republishes; plan proceeds |
385	| fence admitted, crash before replacements, close intervenes | boundary = fence slot; sources terminal; restart issues every unlinked entry once in the new epoch |
386	| replacement issued, crash before the rest | linked entry never re-issued; unlinked entries issued once |
387	| replacements delayed past close while fence admitted | boundary = fence slot; replacements re-planned as new sources; no double apply |
388	| fence delayed past close | boundary unchanged; fence and everything after it re-planned; larger `m` next epoch |
389	| transaction outcome unknown mid-plan | admission halts; reopen enumerates durable truth; no half-link exists |
390	| rollback after adoption | boundaries regress with the closure; linked entries never re-dispositioned |
391	| manual-review entry | no fence, no replacements; only that author stalls |
392	| honest delivery gap (10 delayed, 11 after it) | 11 never admitted without 10; both displaced; plan; fence; advance |
393	| author absent across two or more closes | rows classified by own signature/scope/digest for any old epoch; no hard failure |
394	| fence `m > f`, or `m <= s` | ignored; no abort |
395	| Byzantine fence far ahead | only that author's space burns; recoverable by re-admission on a fresh device |
396	| Byzantine omission of own predecessor | only that author's boundary stalls |
397	| same-slot duplicate | author frozen at prior boundary; close proceeds |
398	| same-key removal and re-entry, same device | new `admissionEpoch`; old rows terminal; first fence at `lineage.next` establishes the base; sequence continues |
399	| same-key re-entry, fresh device | lineage 0; fence or slot 0 accepted; no collision with the old incarnation |
400	| stale old-incarnation vertex delivered | rejected at ingress by anchor; ignored by the scan; no equivocation proof for a cross-anchor pair |
401	| frontier `admissionEpoch` off-rule, boundary regression, vector ≠ successor ACL | rejected by the advance predicate |
402	| cold open with floor trust only and unknown `priorCheckpointDigest` | succeeds; the opener never requests predecessor bytes |
403	| codec given only the successor material's key | verifies; no input exists for a current-epoch key |
404	| control vertex in close graph | in charges/frontier/close-set/history; excluded from the application fold |
405	| row substitution at or below `terminalThrough` | terminal; never applied |
406	| legacy v1 room receives fence/profile | unsupported/mixed-profile rejection; v1 unchanged |
407	| creator's own displaced row | same plan/fence path; no legacy retirement record |
408	| null-boundary member with no fence and no slot 0 | boundary stays null; close succeeds |
409	| prune with an unlinked plan entry | refused |
